## The patronage landscape in Ireland

All primary schools in Ireland are funded by the State, but each one has a patron, and the patron sets the school's ethos. Almost nine in ten have a Catholic patron.

{{< include _patronage-stats.md >}}

<iframe src="../figures/patronage_maps.html" width="100%" height="660" style="border:0" title="Maps of Irish primary schools: denominational and multi-denominational" loading="lazy"></iframe>

**Figure 1.** Mainstream primary schools by patronage. Left: denominational schools, Catholic (blue) and Church of Ireland and other faiths (orange). Right: multi-denominational schools. Hover over or tap a school for its name and county. Inter-denominational schools, run jointly by more than one church, count as denominational. Pupil numbers are each school's enrolment in the same list. Data: Department of Education, [data on individual schools](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-education/collections/data-on-individual-schools/), using the latest list published. Code: [`make_maps.py`](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/blob/main/analysis/charts/make_maps.py). [Open full screen](../figures/patronage_maps.html).

::: {.ethos-cards}
::: {.ethos-card}
### Denominational ethos

- Faith formation in the patron's religion during the school day
- Sacramental preparation in class time (Catholic schools)
- Ethos integrated across the school day; parents may opt children out of religious instruction
:::

::: {.ethos-card .is-multi}
### Multi-denominational ethos

- Ethics and values curriculum (for example Learn Together, or Goodness Me, Goodness You!)
- Learning about religions and beliefs, not formation in one
- Faith formation, where offered, outside school hours or by belief groups
:::
:::
